# Board layout: MTG Arena and other clients, and a buildable spec for Yama

Researched 2026-10-18. Every claim is tagged: **[src]** is backed by a cited page or source file, **[code]** comes from source I read (Forge, XMage, Cockatrice on GitHub; phase's own web client in `/Users/bryanroscoe/Developer/yama-phase/client/src`), and **[unverified]** is my own understanding or a recommendation. Several Wizards pages, mtg.wiki and the Arena support pages returned 403, so a few Arena details rest on secondary guides. Bryan has Arena installed and can confirm the [unverified] Arena items in a minute.

## 0. Key takeaways for Yama

1. **Arena has no 4-player board to copy.** Arena is still 1v1 only. Brawl is 1v1. Wizards has said "We want 3-4 player matches", admitted the interface "was built for two players", and given no date. **[src: Draftsim 2025-08-22; MTGRocks 2024-11-06; Wizards Brawl article 2025-12-15]** So take Arena's *1v1 visual language* (rows, condensed cards, stacks, near-hand commander, examine view, hand drawer). Take the *4-player arrangement* from MTGO, Forge, XMage, Cockatrice, TableCommander and especially phase's own client, which already solves 4-player Commander on the same engine.
2. **Arena's row model** **[src]**: your lands sit bottom-left near you. Non-creature artifacts and enchantments sit bottom-right. Creatures sit in the front row toward the center. Planeswalkers (and sagas) sit far right. The opponent's side is mirrored.
3. **Condensed battlefield cards** **[src]**: Arena shows permanents as small, nearly square rectangles with only name, art and P/T. Full text comes on hover or right-click. Identical cards stack, and token stacks carry a clickable count.
4. **Inspection**: right-click zooms anywhere on desktop (battlefield, stack, graveyard). Long-press zooms on touch. **[src]** Yama already uses tap to filter options, so long-press for inspect fits without a conflict.
5. **Phones** **[src]**: Arena and Hearthstone both tuck the hand into a "drawer" that you tap to fan. Arena auto-tucks it when nothing is playable. Big boards scroll sideways on mobile.
6. **4-player arrangement**: MTGO puts you at the bottom with opponents split across the top half, in clockwise order "up to the left, then all the way across, and then back down to you". **[src]** phase picks "split" (all opponents visible) on desktop and "focused" (one opponent board plus a tab rail) on mobile. **[code]**
7. **Background**: Bryan dislikes felt and likes commander art. Use a neutral dark base with each seat's commander art behind its pane. Scryfall's image rules forbid CSS blur, desaturate or color-shift on card images, and require an artist credit when you show `art_crop`. Details in section 5.7.

---

## 1. MTG Arena (1v1) board anatomy

### 1.1 Screen regions
- **Perspective**: a slight camera tilt gives your side about 60% of the view and the opponent about 40%. **[src: GDKeys]**
- **Flow**: the board follows a left-to-right flow. Deck, discard and action buttons sit in the corners. The middle stays wide and mostly empty, because big boards need several rows. **[src: GDKeys]**
- **Opponent's corner**: kept minimal, showing only turn, life and hand count. **[src: GDKeys]**
- **Bottom (you)** **[src: Hipsters of the Coast 2018; Draftsim]**:
  - The hand is bottom-center with the lower halves of the cards off-screen. Hover lifts a card. Playable cards get a blue outline.
  - The phase strip sits above the hand. Your avatar is in the middle of it, with life just below.
  - Phase stops are icons beside each avatar. Orange means a stop on your turn, blue a stop on the opponent's turn. **[src: MTG Arena Zone]**
  - Pass and End Turn are bottom-right, with timeouts (an hourglass) above them.
  - The settings gear is top-right. **[src: Beginner's Guide site]**
- **Piles**: library, graveyard and exile were described left of the hand in 2018. Newer guides describe small icons under the avatar showing graveyard and exile counts; clicking one opens a panel to the left of the battlefield. **[src]** Exact current placement: **[unverified, check in client]**
- **Stack and emblems**: emblems sit on the left and the stack on the right. Arrows let you shift them aside to reach cards underneath. **[src: Beginner's Guide site]**
  - Cards on the stack are auto-zoomed. **[src: Draftsim tips]**
  - Spells on the stack are tinted the same color as their targeting arrows, and multiple target groups get different colors. **[src: Arena 0.09 patch notes]** This is worth copying.
- **No full game log.** Players complain they can't review what happened. **[src: Steam thread]** Yama's replay log is already ahead here.

### 1.2 Battlefield rows **[src: Hipsters 2018; mtg.wiki summary via search; Draftsim mobile]**

| Row | Your side | Opponent's side (mirrored) |
|---|---|---|
| Front, toward the center | Creatures | Creatures |
| Back, near your edge | Lands on the left; non-creature artifacts and enchantments on the right | Same, along their edge |
| Far right | Planeswalkers and sagas, in their own zone (it pages instead of overflowing) | Same |

- **Battles** stay horizontal and sit on the *protector's* side. Wizards playtested both sides and chose this because combat felt right. **[src: Wizards "We Put Battles on MTG Arena"]**
- **Planeswalker zone**: Wizards rebuilt it so permanents don't "page off the screen". **[src: same]** So this zone pages rather than shrinking.

### 1.3 Condensed cards, stacks and crowding
- **Condensed cards** **[src]**: nearly square; name, art and P/T only. Keyword ability icons exist in Arena's symbol set (flying, deathtouch, first strike and so on). **[src: Arena wiki/symbol listings]** Exactly where they sit on battlefield cards: **[unverified]**
- **Status badges** **[src: patch notes 2026.58.0 via search]**: Arena adds badges for special states, for example a spellbook graphic on a creature with a prepared spell, and a converge badge that fills by colors spent. There is also a summoning-sickness visual effect. **[src: 0.09 patch notes]**
- **Stacking**: identical cards stack. **[src: GDKeys]**
  - Tokens stack with a number. "Click on the number of the tokens once they're stacked to have them all attack at a single target." **[src: Draftsim tips]**
  - Planeswalker tokens can be attacked individually. Legendary planeswalkers don't stack. **[src: patch notes]**
  - Arena caps each player at 250 tokens. **[src: Dec 2020 notes]**
- **Crowding**: cards shrink as the board fills. On mobile, "scroll to the side so you can see the entire battlefield at a reasonable scale". Names get hard to read but P/T stays clear. **[src: Draftsim mobile]**

### 1.4 Brawl and command zone display **[src: MTG Arena Zone Brawl guide (2019); Draftsim Brawl guide (2025)]**
- While your commander is in the command zone, it appears as a **"near-hand" castable**, a card shown beside your hand.
- The opponent's commander is also visible.
- Each player's commander name is listed under their name, and clicking it enlarges the card.
- On the battlefield, a commander has a distinct border.
- Commander tax is not a standing counter. The card's displayed cost updates, and you hover to see the final cost.

### 1.5 Inspection and input
- **Desktop**: right-click zooms everywhere, and the zoom shows flavor text beside the card. **[src]**
- **Touch**: Wizards describes "Examined (hover or long-press) views". **[src: Battles article]**
- **Hotkeys** **[src]**:
  - Space: pass priority.
  - Enter: pass until something happens.
  - Shift+Enter: pass the turn.
  - Ctrl: full control for now. Ctrl+Shift: hold full control.
  - Z: undo mana.
  - QQ: float all mana. Hold Q: tap all lands of one name.
  - L: show phases.
- **Zone hotkeys**, as listed by the AccessibleArena screen-reader mod (useful because they show Arena's internal zone model):
  - C hand, G graveyard, X exile, S stack, W command zone.
  - Battlefield rows: B creatures, A lands, R non-creatures.
- **Mobile**: hold your avatar to enter full control. **[src]**

### 1.6 Arena on phones and tablets **[src: SCG / Wizards mobile features guide; Wargamer; Draftsim mobile]**
- The hand uses "a tap to view system", so you can zoom or minimize it at will. You can also tap the hand to fan it.
- An automatic "tuck" hides the hand when you can't play anything.
- Avatars were shrunk and moved for phone screens.
- Tablets look essentially like desktop.
- Phones are landscape-only. **[unverified]**
- The stack is the weak spot: hard to read when full, with items "piled atop one another".

---

## 2. How other clients handle 4-player boards

| Client | Arrangement | Notable details |
|---|---|---|
| **MTGO** (Commander, up to 4) **[src: mtgo.com multiplayer guide]** | You at the bottom; opponents split across the top half. | Turn order runs clockwise: up to the left, across, back down to you. The battlefield highlight follows **priority**, not the active player. Each opponent section has a +/- button to hide them, which enlarges the rest. Opponents' cards shrink to fit, and the guide says "use Hover Zoom liberally". A shield icon in your avatar shows commander damage; right-click lists its sources. Zones toggle open and closed. Cards exiled by a permanent "appear underneath the permanent that exiled them". |
| **XMage** **[code: `GamePanel.addPlayers`]** | Seats in a circle on 2 rows. Columns = ceil(n/2). You at bottom-left, the next seats to your right along the bottom, then the top row right-to-left (clockwise). With an odd number, you span 2 columns. | A player who leaves collapses to a 95px strip and the others get the width. Card layout: stacks of up to 5, with offsets of 7% of width (x) and 10% of height (y); attachments sit 13% of height below their host **[code: `CardPluginImpl`]**. |
| **Forge desktop** **[code: `PlayArea.java`]** | One dockable panel per player. | Rows are Land (non-creature lands), Token, Creature, Contraption and Other. Opponents are mirrored: lands at the far edge, creatures nearest the center. You get creatures, then tokens, then lands at the bottom. "Others" align right and fill leftover space in existing rows before getting a row of their own. **Fit**: binary search on card width between max 300px and min 50px until every row fits; at the minimum width it scrolls. **Stacks**: offset 12% x and 12% y; depth default 4 (setting 1-10). In group mode, cards past that depth are hidden and the top card shows a count badge; clicking the badge or shift-clicking selects the whole group. Cards exiled by a permanent render as "ghost" cards attached to it. Combat: attackers and blockers are sorted by the screen x position of the creature they face, so the combat lines don't cross. |
| **Forge mobile** **[code: `MatchScreen.java`, `VField.java`]** | Portrait: players stacked vertically in a scroll view. | Each player gets 2 card rows (3 when a zone tab is open). Avatars are halved for 3-4 players. Pinch zoom adds height. Row 1 holds creatures (or other permanents if there are no creatures); row 2 holds lands plus others and is shortened by the command zone's width on the right. Card slots are square so tapped cards fit. Eliminated players' panels are removed in landscape. |
| **Cockatrice** **[code: `game_scene.cpp`]** | One column below a player-count threshold (a setting), otherwise 2 columns. | You are the bottom row of the first column. Every board except the bottom row is mirrored so it faces the center. The phase toolbar runs down the left side. |
| **phase client** (local fork) **[code]** | `"auto"` resolves to `"split"` on desktop and `"focused"` on mobile (`gameStateView.ts`). Split puts all opponents in a top grid with one column each, taking 60% of height. Focused shows one mirrored opponent board plus an opponent tab rail. | Seat panes have a header, a peeking hand fan, a pile rail and a seat-color tint. The active seat gets a rose glow; a seat being waited on gets an amber pulse chip. Tabs: clicking the body focuses that board; clicking the avatar targets that player. Tabs show a crosshair when the player is a legal target, a red ⚔×N badge for attackers coming at you (hover shows mini cards), and a board-peek popover while you're choosing targets. An option follows the active opponent. A compact/comfortable density toggle is included. |
| **TableCommander** (web VTT) **[src: its docs]** | Four view modes on keys 1-4: Single, Side-by-side, Stacked, Quadrant. Tab cycles boards. | Eliminated boards stay until hidden, then reflow (a quadrant with one player out becomes two over one). Two bands: creatures/enchantments above lands. The zone column is on the right; commander tax "lives on the zone". Token stacks carry a count badge with split and remove actions. Hover preview lists counters. |
| **SpellTable / playgroup.gg** **[src]** | SpellTable shows all four boards at once or one at a time. playgroup.gg shows the whole table on laptop and tablet, and "one player at a time" in landscape on phones. | playgroup.gg puts attached cards on a shelf next to the creature they enchant. |
| **untap.in** **[src: Draftsim 2026]** | Freeform tabletop. | No rules automation, no step tracker, tokens added by hand. Its wiki's interface guide is empty, so I couldn't document the layout. Low value as a reference. |
| **Hearthstone** (genre UX) **[src: GDKeys; hearthstone.wiki.gg; phone-launch press]** | Hero bottom-center and top-center; one minion row capped at 7. | History column on the left (about 7-10 recent actions, blue border for yours and red for the opponent's, hover for detail). Deck on the right; mana bottom-right. On phones only the top half of the hand shows; tap to open the "hand drawer", tap-and-hold for one card's detail. Battlegrounds keeps an always-visible leaderboard of all 8 players on the left. |

---

## 3. Algorithms to borrow

### 3.1 Group key: when two permanents may share a stack
phase's `groupKey` (`viewmodel/battlefieldProps.ts`) **[code]** is the most complete. Two permanents stack only if all of these match:
- name, tapped, face_down, flipped, transformed
- power, toughness, loyalty, damage_marked
- has_summoning_sickness, class_level, colors
- sorted keywords, rendered counters
- token rules text, token art preset, is_token, is_commander

A permanent is never grouped if it has attachments, is the ring-bearer, is face-down or is melded.

Forge and XMage use the same idea, and both also refuse to stack tokens with non-tokens.

**Yama today** keeps tapped and untapped copies of a land in one pile with an "n tapped" label, and only stacks lands. Change this:
- Split tapped and untapped into separate stacks, so the rotation itself shows tapped state, as Arena and Forge do.
- Stack creatures, tokens and others too.

### 3.2 How a group renders
phase `groupRenderMode.ts` **[code]**:

| Count | Render |
|---|---|
| 1 | single card |
| 2-4 | "staggered": offsets of 20px (creatures), 10px (lands), 14px (others) |
| 5 or more | collapsed to one card with a ×N badge |

- A manual "expand" shows every member.
- During declare blockers, a group containing an attacker you can block auto-expands, unless it has 5 or more members; then members are reached through a picker.
- Forge uses offsets of 12% of card width and default depth 4. XMage uses 7%/10% and depth 5.
- Clicking a badge selects the whole stack. Both Arena and Forge do this.

### 3.3 Crowding
- **Forge (desktop)**: binary-search one card width for the whole area so every row fits without scrolling, between 300 and 50px; scroll only at the floor.
- **phase** (`BattlefieldZoneOverflow.tsx`, `BattlefieldRow.tsx`) **[code]**:
  - Count **distinct stacks**, not cards.
  - Lands or others collapse into a **summary tile** past 8 stacks on desktop, 4 on mobile, or 4 in a split opponent pane. The tile shows untapped mana pips by color (W U B R G C) and type counts. Tapping it opens a drawer.
  - Creatures turn into a scrollable grid past 12 stacks (desktop) or 6 (mobile). Creatures in combat sort to the front, and fades plus a chevron show there's more.
  - Minimum readable card height before wrapping to two rows: 80px full-width, 56px on short (landscape-phone) screens, 44px in split panes.
- **Arena**: shrink cards, scroll sideways on mobile, and page the planeswalker zone.

### 3.4 Row order and mirroring
- **You** (top to bottom): creatures (toward the center), then lands on the left with others on the right.
- **Opponents**: the same rows flipped, so creatures face the center.
- Cockatrice, Forge and phase all mirror every board except yours.

### 3.5 Combat
- Group attackers by defending player (phase `groupAttackersByTarget`).
- Sort your creatures to line up against the attackers they block (phase `sortCreaturesForBlockers`; Forge sorts by the opponent creature's x position).
- Draw lines from attackers to the attacked player or permanent. Color-match them with the stack item, as Arena does.

### 3.6 Eliminated players
Collapse their pane to a thin strip (XMage uses 95px) and reflow the others; TableCommander turns a quadrant into two over one. Don't flip the layout to 1v1 when only two players remain: phase keys "is 1v1" on seat count, not on live players.

---

## 4. What Yama's View is missing for this
Yama's `CardView` (`/Users/bryanroscoe/Developer/yama/web/src/play/types.ts`) has name, tapped, P/T, loyalty, damage, counters, types and an untyped `attached_to`.

phase's filtered state already carries more (`/Users/bryanroscoe/Developer/yama-phase/client/src/adapter/types.ts`): `keywords` and `base_keywords`, `has_summoning_sickness`, `is_token`, `is_commander`, `commander_tax`, `attachments`, `attached_to`, `face_down`, `color`, `exile_links` (exiled_id → source_id), and `derived.commander_damage_by_attacker`.

Forward these through `play/` into Yama's View for:
- stacking (section 3.1)
- keyword icons
- a summoning-sick marker
- the commander border and tax chip
- attachments fanned under their host
- "exiled with" cards shown under their source

Caution: respect the hidden-information rule in ARCHITECTURE. Face-down exiled cards must not reveal names to other seats. **[unverified, how phase filters exile links per viewer]**

For card art, Scryfall now has WEBP formats: `art` (626×457, replaces `art_crop`), `grid` (488×680), `display` (672×936) and `thumb`. **[src: Scryfall Card Imagery docs]**

---

## 5. Recommended Yama spec (to build or to hand to the design session)

### 5.1 Desktop, 4 players (≥1280×800, landscape)
```
grid-template-rows: minmax(0,38fr) auto minmax(0,40fr) auto
grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 340px      /* right rail: stack, options, log */
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────┐
│ Opp LEFT (next)    │ Opp ACROSS        │ Opp RIGHT (prev)  │ STACK  │
│ header (art bg)    │ header            │ header            │ (auto- │
│ lands | others row │ lands | others    │ lands | others    │ zoom   │
│ creatures row ↓    │ creatures ↓       │ creatures ↓       │ top)   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ OPTIONS│
│ phase track · combat arrows · "Attacking you: 3"          │ chips  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ + Pass │
│ your creatures row ↑                          │ PW / sagas│ recent │
│ lands (left) ……………… artifacts/enchantments (right)        │ log    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────┤
│ lib·gy·ex │ commander (near-hand) │  hand fan  │ avatar+life │ Pass│
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- **Seat order**: opponents left to right in turn order after you, as MTGO does. The left pane is the next player.
- **Focus**: clicking an opponent header widens that pane to about 60%. The other two become compact strips showing header, mana summary and creature count, like phase's "focused" mode, MTGO's +/- and TableCommander's Side-by-side.
- **Keyboard**: 1-4 for view modes and Tab to cycle focus. **[unverified recommendation]**
- **Active and waiting state**: the active turn gets a colored ring and a "Turn" label. A seat being waited on gets an amber pulsing "deciding…" (Yama already has this). Also highlight the seat with priority, as MTGO does.
- **Hand**: a fan of overlapping cards bottom-center, about 60% visible, lifting to full size on hover. Playable cards glow (Yama already has `.playable`).
- **Commander**: shown left of the hand as a near-hand castable with tax applied to the cost, as in Arena Brawl.

### 5.2 Phone, portrait (Yama's installable app, about 390×844)
```
[ opponent tab rail: 3 tabs ]                                  ~56px
  each tab: round commander-art avatar, name, life, turn ring,
  ⚔N badge, target crosshair; tap = focus, tap avatar = target
[ focused opponent board (mirrored): header + 2 rows ]         ~30%
[ phase pill · stack chip (count, tap = sheet) · combat ]      ~32px
[ your board: creatures row / lands+others row ]               ~30%
[ decision bar: prompt + chips + Pass ]                        auto
[ hand drawer: 40% peek; tap = fan; auto-tuck when nothing's playable ]
```
- Follow the active opponent by default, as phase does, but don't steal focus while the user is choosing a target. Add a pin to turn it off.
- Long-press any card to open the inspector sheet; tap keeps its current job (filter options). Arena and Hearthstone both use long-press or hold for detail.
- Rows don't wrap. Lands and others collapse to a mana-pip summary tile past 4 stacks; creatures become a horizontal scroller past 6 stacks.
- Offer landscape as an option, which matches playgroup.gg ("one player at a time") and phase's compact-height rules.

### 5.3 Seat pane anatomy (opponent)
**Header** (about 56px desktop, 44px phone), over the commander art:
- name
- **life**, the largest number in the header (28-32px desktop)
- poison, shown only if above 0
- hand count, library count
- graveyard chip (count plus top-card thumbnail) and exile chip (shown only if above 0); tapping either opens a browser sheet
- commander chip: art thumbnail, "Tax +N", and commander damage *to you*

**Body**:
- creature row nearest the center
- lands (left) and others (right) at the far edge

### 5.4 Battlefield tile anatomy (Arena-style condensed card)
- **Shape**: near-square, art-forward. Use `art` WEBP or `art_crop` as the face.
- **Text**: draw the name, P/T and badges as HTML, not as tiny printed text.
  - Name bar at the top: one line, ellipsis, 11-12px minimum.
  - P/T box bottom-right, bold. **[unverified recommendation]** Show it green above base and red when lower or damaged; Yama already marks damage.
  - Loyalty in a shield shape.
  - Counters as pills.
  - Keyword icon column with a "+N" overflow cap. phase uses the `mana-font` `ms-ability-*` glyphs (flying, reach, deathtouch and so on; `keywordProps.ts`).
  - A small "zzz" or desaturated frame for summoning sickness. Make it a separate overlay element, not a CSS filter on the art (see section 5.7).
- **Commander**: distinct border, as in Arena.
- **Tapped**: rotate 90°. Use square slots so rotation doesn't change the row height, as Forge mobile does.
- **Attachments**: fan out behind the host, peeking about 13% of its height (XMage).
- **Exiled-with cards**: show as small ghost cards under the source (MTGO, Forge).
- **Full card** on hover (desktop), right-click (examine), or long-press (touch). Showing the full card image in the inspector also satisfies Scryfall's credit rule for the art crop.

### 5.5 Stack and log
- The stack lives in the right rail on desktop and as a bottom-sheet chip on phones. The top item is shown large; the rest are a list.
- Color each stack item and its target arrows the same, as Arena does.
- Keep Yama's replay log. A Hearthstone-style recent-actions strip (last 7-10, colored by seat, hover for detail) is a cheap win, since Arena has no log at all.

### 5.6 Inspector (examine view)
Contents: large image, Oracle text, current P/T versus printed, counters, keyword reminders, attached cards, "exiled with" cards, and the options for this card (Yama already has these).

Opening it:
- Desktop: right-click or the Read button.
- Touch: long-press.
- Esc closes it.

### 5.7 Background and commander art (Bryan's preference)
- **Base**: a neutral dark slate in place of the `--felt*` variables in `/Users/bryanroscoe/Developer/yama/web/src/play/board.css`. **[unverified color choice]**
- **Each seat pane**: its commander's art fills the header and fades into the pane. Mythic Tools does this; phase tints panes by seat color.
- **Scryfall rules** **[src: Scryfall API overview]**:
  - "Do not blur, sharpen, desaturate, or color-shift card images."
  - "Do not distort, skew, or stretch."
  - When using the art crop, "list the artist name and copyright elsewhere in the same interface", or show the full card image elsewhere in the same interface.
- **So**: never put CSS `filter` on the art. For text contrast, lay a *separate* gradient element over it, and show "Art: <artist>" in the seat header. The commander card in the inspector also covers the credit.
- `object-fit: cover` crops the art crop further. Yama's ARCHITECTURE says "no cropping or recoloring", which is stricter than Scryfall, so decide whether `cover` is acceptable or use `contain` on a matching dark field. **[judgment call for Bryan]**

---

## 6. Gaps and things to check in Arena
- Current positions of Arena's library, graveyard and exile piles (sources disagree between "left of hand" in 2018 and "icons under the avatar").
- Whether phone Arena is landscape-only.
- Where keyword icons sit on Arena battlefield cards, and whether P/T changes color when buffed.
- MTGO's land and token grouping rules: I found no text source.
- untap.in's actual multiplayer layout: its docs are empty.
- Arena's 2026 State of the Game: I could not find it, so I can't rule out a late-2026 multiplayer announcement. The newest sources I found (Aug-Dec 2025) give no date.

findings.findings_markdown:
## Main findings

1. **The option list can't do everything Arena does.** Yama submits only an index into `AiDecisionContract.candidates` (`play/src/lib.rs` `Match::choose`). For any choice with many possible answers, that list is a pruned sample made for the AI, not the full set of legal moves. Verified in `../yama-phase/crates/engine/src/ai_support/candidates.rs`:
   - **Attacks** (`attacker_actions`): the only options are no attack, one creature at one target, or an alpha strike at one target. You can't send 2 of your 4 creatures at Ana.
   - **Blocks:** single blocks plus gang blocks against menace. You can't make two separate blocks at once.
   - **Scry and surveil** (`select_cards_variants`): none, all, or a single card. With scry 3 you can't keep 2 on top.
   - **Trigger order:** every order is listed only for 4 triggers or fewer. With 5 or more, only identity and reverse.
   - **Combat damage:** only the greedy split.
   - **Library searches for 2+ cards:** the pool is capped at 12 cards (`ENGINE_CANDIDATE_CAP`). The engine's own comment says: "Player submissions are validated by the engine submission guard, not by this enumeration."
   - Combat is the one exception: `AiDecisionContract::contains_action` accepts **any** declaration that passes `validate_attack_declaration` / `validate_blockers_for_player`. Click-to-attack and drag-to-block can be submitted through the existing contract path, just not by index.
2. **The engine already has most of Arena's priority features built in.** In `types/actions.rs` and `types/game_state.rs`:
   - `SetPriorityPassingMode` (`Standard | SkipLowUseWindows | FullControl`).
   - `SetPhaseStops` (`{phase, scope: AllTurns|OwnTurn|OpponentsTurns}`).
   - `SetAutoPass` (`UntilStackEmpty` = "Resolve"; `UntilTurnBoundary{EndOfCurrentTurn|MyNextTurnStart}` = pass turn). There is also `CancelAutoPass`.
   - `SetPriorityYield` (auto-pass one trigger, either this copy or all copies).
   - `SetMayTriggerAutoChoice`, `SetTriggerOrderTemplate`, `SetReplacementAutoChoice` (the "don't ask again" choices).
   - `BeginResolveAll{scope: Own|Shared}`.
   - Mana payment:
     - The mode is chosen when casting: `CastSpell{payment_mode: Auto|AutoExceptSacrificialMana|Manual}`.
     - Tapping and undoing taps: `TapLandForMana`/`ActivateManaSource`, `UntapLandForMana` (the undo), `SpendPoolMana`/`UnspendPoolMana`.
     - At `ManaPayment`, `PassPriority` means "pay the rest automatically". `CancelCast` backs out.
   - `ReorderHand`.
   - `auto_pass_recommended_for_viewer` is the engine's ladder, commented as "MTGA-style": your own object on top auto-resolves, opponent-turn holds only if you can actually cast something, and so on.
   - The preference actions are "legal in any WaitingFor state" and apply only to the player who sends them.
   - Yama's own `should_auto_pass` duplicates a thinner version of this.
3. **phase's own client (MIT, `../yama-phase/client/src/components`) already has working versions of most screens below.** It is worth reading, or borrowing from with attribution:
   - Targeting: `targeting/TargetingOverlay.tsx`, `arcPath.ts`.
   - Phase stops: `controls/PhaseStopBar.tsx`.
   - Mana: `mana/ManaPaymentUI.tsx`, `ChooseXValueUI.tsx`.
   - Combat damage: `combat/DamageAssignmentModal.tsx`.
   - Triggers: `modal/TriggerOrderModal.tsx`.
   - Scry, surveil, dig and search: `modal/cardChoice/libraryModals.tsx`.
   - Stack: `stack/StackDisplay.tsx`, `StackTargetArcs.tsx`.
   - Drag to cast: `hooks/useDragToCast.ts`.
   - Button labels: `client/src/i18n/locales/en/game.json`.

## Protocol change this needs

- **New client message:** `{type:"act", revision, action:<GameAction JSON>}`.
  - Only allow listed action types: `DeclareAttackers`, `DeclareBlockers`, `SelectCards`, `OrderTriggers`, `AssignCombatDamage`, `DistributeAmong`, `ChooseX`, `SelectModes`, the mana actions above, `CancelCast`, and `CastSpell` with a payment mode.
  - Server side: check that the seat is in `waiting_for.acting_players()` and that the revision matches.
  - Combat: submit through `apply_ai_action_proposal` with a freshly issued contract.
  - Everything else: use `engine::game::engine::apply` (the same call `concede` uses). Then `log.push_action` so replays stay deterministic.
- **Preference message:** `{type:"prefs", action}` for `SetPhaseStops`, `SetPriorityPassingMode`, `SetAutoPass`, `CancelAutoPass`, `SetPriorityYield`, `ReorderHand`.
  - These must also go into the replay log, because the engine takes auto-passes that never reach a client.
- **New fields in the view:**
  - A typed, per-seat-filtered `prompt` (the `WaitingFor` payload). Send it only to the deciding seat. `SearchChoice`, `ScryChoice` and `DigChoice` name hidden cards, and ARCHITECTURE.md's rule about never sending raw engine state still applies.
  - `by_object: {objectId: optionIndex[]}`, built from `legal_actions_full().legal_actions_by_object`. That map includes mana abilities, which the flat list leaves out.
  - `prefs` (stops and passing mode).
  - `auto_pass` (the active session, so the button can say "Passing to end of turn, Cancel").
  - `deadline_ms` (for a timer).
- **Keep the index buttons.** They are the fallback that always works for every decision type.

## Arena interaction model and what to build

How sure each claim is: **[S]** means a source is listed below. **[M]** is from memory of the Arena client; Bryan should check it in Arena.

### 1. The main button and passing priority
- **How Arena works:**
  - A large orange button sits bottom-right. Space presses it. [S]
  - Enter passes until something happens you can respond to, and it doesn't stop for triggers. [S]
  - Shift+Enter passes the whole turn; you only get priority back to block. Pressing Enter again, or clicking the small orange arrow bottom-right, turns it off. [S]
  - Verified labels: "Keep" / "Mulligan" [S], "All Attack", which becomes "1 Attacker" etc. [S], "Done" [S]. Other labels: "Next", "Pass", "Resolve", "End Turn", "No Attacks", "No Blocks", "Cancel", "Submit". [M]
  - Without full control, Arena passes for you when you have no play, including straight after a land drop. Setting a stop on Main 1 or Main 2 prevents that. [S]
- **Build:** one primary button and one contextual secondary button.
  - Desktop: bottom-right above the hand. Phone: right end of the dock, within thumb reach.
  - Primary label by state:
    - Stack not empty: "Resolve".
    - Your main 1: "To combat" (if you have attackers), otherwise "Next".
    - Main 2 or end step: "End turn".
    - Opponent's turn: "Pass".
    - Declare attackers: "Attack (3)" / "No attacks".
    - Declare blockers: "Block (2)" / "No blocks".
    - Targeting with a variable count: "Done (2/3)".
    - Waiting: disabled "Waiting for Ana", with her portrait.
  - Secondary button: "Attack with all", "Reset blocks", or "Resolve all" (when 2+ stack items).
  - Next to it, a small toggle for passing the turn: `SetAutoPass{UntilTurnBoundary{EndOfCurrentTurn}}`, cancelled with `CancelAutoPass`.

### 2. Phase stops
- **How Arena works:**
  - Click a step icon on the timeline next to your portrait or your opponent's. Orange means a stop on your turn; blue means a stop on the opponent's turn. [S]
  - Icons: Upkeep/Draw, Main 1, Combat (beginning), Declare Attackers (single sword), Declare Blockers (shield), Damage (explosion), Main 2, end step ("After This Turn"). [S]
  - A stop works like full control for that step, and it still fires while "Pass Turn" is on. [S]
  - L shows or hides the phase icons. [S]
  - Separate one-off stops for the current turn sit bottom-right. [S]
  - Sources disagree on whether ladder stops persist or reset each turn. [S, conflicting]
- **Build for Commander:** Arena is 1v1. phase's scopes fit 4 players.
  - Ladder beside **my** portrait: my-turn stops (`OwnTurn`).
  - Ladder beside **the active opponent's** portrait: opponents'-turn stops (`OpponentsTurns`), applying to all opponents.
  - Clicking cycles off → my turns → opponents' turns → all turns. phase's `PhaseStopBar` uses this order.
  - Hide Untap and Cleanup.
  - Keep two kinds of stop: standing stops, saved per user across games, and "this turn only" stops that Yama clears at turn end.
  - Use two hues **plus** a shape cue for colour-blind players. No felt green.
  - Per-opponent stops would need Yama server logic; the engine doesn't support them.
- **Phone:** a phase chip that opens a sheet. phase's `MobilePhaseChip` uses scope pills: Off / All turns / My turns / Opponents' turns.

### 3. Full control, auto-pass, yields, Resolve All
- **How Arena works:**
  - Ctrl turns on full control: you get priority at every step, including before your triggers resolve. It turns off after you pass. [S]
  - Ctrl+Shift locks full control on until you turn it off. [S]
  - Phone: press and hold your own avatar. [S, official FAQ]
  - Full control also takes over from Auto Tap, so you pay manually. [S]
  - No documented "Resolve all". Players complain about clicking through about 20 lifegain triggers one at a time. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Replace `should_auto_pass` with the engine's version: `SetPriorityPassingMode` plus `auto_pass_recommended_for_viewer`. Keep Yama's server loop that submits `PassPriority`.
  - The engine comment says `FullControl` must live in engine state, so that Resolve All sessions started by other players respect it.
  - Ctrl and long-press avatar: temporary full control (Yama turns it back off after one pass). Ctrl+Shift: locked.
  - Show a visible "Full control" pill whenever it's on.
  - Stack items get "Auto-pass this trigger": either just this copy or all copies (`SetPriorityYield`). This goes beyond Arena but helps a lot with Commander's repeated triggers.
  - "Resolve all" uses `BeginResolveAll{scope:Own}`. It covers only your own passes, asks nobody, and is interrupted by stops or required choices.
  - Use `Shared` (the whole table must agree) only for loop shortcuts.

### 4. Casting from hand
- **How Arena works:**
  - Three ways to play a card: drag up and release, double-click, or click, release, click. [S, WotC_Jay]
  - Playable cards have a blue outline. [S]
  - Cards you can cast from graveyard or exile sit beside the hand, set apart by a gap. [S]
  - Changed costs get a halo. [S]
  - Hovering a spell, or dragging it without dropping, highlights the lands Auto Tap would use. [S]
  - Phone: a tap acts as a left click and a long-press as a right click (inspect). Tap the hand to fan it. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Hand behaviour:
    - The hand is fanned.
    - Hovering raises a card to full size.
    - Playable cards glow, using `by_object`.
  - Drag:
    - It starts after the pointer moves 6px.
    - The card follows the pointer at full size.
    - Crossing a play line about 64px above the hand band arms the drop. phase uses `HAND_DRAG_PLAY_THRESHOLD = -64` for the hand and `-20` elsewhere.
    - Releasing above the line submits the card's only play action. If there are several (adventure, MDFC face, flashback, alternative cost), a small popover opens at the drop point.
    - Releasing below the line snaps the card back. Esc cancels.
  - Double-click does the same as a drop.
  - Single click selects the card and filters the action strip, which is Yama's current behaviour.
  - Phone:
    - Tap opens the card sheet, as today.
    - Flicking up 64px or more plays the card.
    - Long-press opens the inspector.
  - Later: a server call `preview_payment(option)` that returns the source ids `auto_tap_mana_sources` would pick, so those lands can glow while a card is held over the battlefield.

### 5. Targeting
- **How Arena works:**
  - An arrow runs from the spell to the cursor. [M]
  - The card's text is coloured to match the targeting line. [S]
  - Abilities auto-pick their only legal target. Spells always make you click one ("When casting a spell, we like to make sure there's at least one choice you're making"). [S, WotC_Jay]
  - Hovering a stack item shows its targets. [S]
  - Z undoes wrong targets before the spell finishes casting. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Engine data: `WaitingFor::TargetSelection{target_slots, mode_labels, selection{current_slot, current_legal_targets}}`.
  - Overlay:
    - A fixed SVG layer that ignores pointer events.
    - The curve is a quadratic Bezier with its control point offset by `min(80, 0.3*dist)` perpendicular to the line (`arcPath.ts`).
    - It is dashed and animated while aiming, solid once locked.
  - Targets:
    - Legal targets get a glow ring and lift slightly.
    - Everything else dims to 40% and can't be clicked.
    - Opponents' commander-art panels act as player targets.
  - A banner at top centre: "Choose target creature or player (1 of 2)", plus the mode label for modal spells.
  - Chosen targets get numbered badges. "Done" lights up once the minimum is met.
  - When a trigger's target step (`TriggerTargetSelection`) has exactly one legal choice, the server picks it automatically. Spells (`TargetSelection`) always ask.
  - Esc, right-click or "Cancel" sends `CancelCast` (only when `allows_cancel_cast()`).
  - Phone: tap the target directly; the arrow is drawn afterwards as feedback.

### 6. Modes and X
- **How Arena works:** each mode shows as its own tile, and X uses an up/down number picker. [M]
- **Build:**
  - Modes:
    - Data: `ModeChoice` / `AbilityModeChoice.mode_descriptions`, answered with `SelectModes{indices}`.
    - Each mode is a tile with its text.
    - "Choose two" is multi-select with a counter.
  - X:
    - Data: `ChooseXValue{min,max,x_cost_previews}`, answered with `ChooseX`.
    - Today Yama shows one button per X value. Replace that with a stepper: minus/plus, a number field, a "Max" button, and digit keys.
    - Show the engine's total cost next to it, e.g. "X=4 -> {4}{R}{R}", from `x_cost_previews`.
    - Default to the largest X you can afford.

### 7. Mana payment
- **How Arena works:**
  - The Auto Tap setting can only be changed during a match. [S]
  - You can always tap lands yourself and click mana in the pool to spend it. [S]
  - Z undoes taps. [S]
  - QQ taps every non-creature mana source into your pool ("float all"). [S]
  - Holding Q and clicking taps every land with the same name. [S]
  - An AutoTap button appears when AutoTap isn't paying for you (convoke, sacrificing a Treasure, or AutoTap off). Hovering it previews what it will use; clicking pays the whole cost. [S, patch 0.14, April 2019]
  - Known AutoTap weak spots: utility lands, colour-heavy hands, cost reducers. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Setting "Tap mana for me":
    - Default `AutoExceptSacrificialMana`, so it never sacrifices a Treasure without asking.
    - `Auto` as an option.
    - `Manual` whenever full control is on.
  - Payment panel (shown at `ManaPayment`, anchored above the hand):
    - Cost pips fill in as you pay.
    - Usable sources glow.
    - Click a land: `TapLandForMana`. Click it again: `UntapLandForMana`, which only works while that mana is unspent.
    - Pool chips like "2x{G} from Forest" can be clicked to choose which pool mana gets spent (`SpendPoolMana`).
    - "Auto-pay rest" sends `PassPriority`, with a hover preview.
    - "Cancel" sends `CancelCast`.
    - `ManaSourceSelection` asks before sacrificing a mana source.
  - Allow floating mana during normal priority (mana abilities come through `by_object`). Z undoes.
  - Later: QQ and Q-hold shortcuts.

### 8. Timers and the rope
- **How Arena works** (community sources; the numbers may be out of date):
  - Each action adds time. When time runs low, a burning rope appears. One source says it appears about a minute in and burns for about 45 seconds. [S]
  - Playing 3 turns without the rope earns one extension, shown as 3 dots and an hourglass. An extension is used up automatically when the rope burns out. With none left, you are forced to pass priority. [S]
  - Best-of-three matches have 30 minutes in total. [S]
  - Opponents' stack items show for at least 0.4 seconds. [S]
  - Roping is reportable. [S]
- **Build for a friends' table:**
  - Off by default. A table timer can be turned on in the lobby.
  - The server holds the deadline (`deadline_ms` in the view). The rope burns around the deciding player's portrait and the primary button for the last 30 seconds.
  - When it runs out: auto-pass if it was a priority window. If a required decision is pending, don't pick for the player; offer the host "Let AI play this seat" (Yama already has AI seats).
  - Other players get a "Nudge" button.
  - AI actions and new stack items get 400–700ms of pacing so people can follow what happened.

### 9. Declaring attackers
- **How Arena works:**
  - Click (phone: tap) creatures to toggle them as attackers. [S, official FAQ]
  - "All Attack" changes to "N Attacker(s)". Must-attack creatures are no longer selected in advance. [S]
  - You are then asked for each attacker's target (player, planeswalker or battle). You can also click several creatures and then their target. [S]
  - Clicking the count on a token pile sends the whole pile. [S]
  - Hovering the defending player shows unblocked attackers. [S]
- **Build** (the data is `DeclareAttackers{valid_attacker_ids, valid_attack_targets_by_attacker, attacker_constraints}`):
  - Picking attackers and defenders:
    - Clicking toggles an attacker. It slides forward and shows a badge with its defender's commander-art thumbnail.
    - If there's only one legal defender, it's assigned automatically. Otherwise the last defender you picked is reused; if there isn't one, the defender row pulses and you click a portrait or planeswalker.
    - Dragging an attacker onto a portrait selects it and assigns that defender in one move.
  - Shortcuts:
    - "Attack with all" opens a choice with "All at Ana / Ben / Cat" and "Split...".
    - The pile count chip toggles the whole pile.
  - Requirements and confirming:
    - "Must attack" badges come from `attacker_constraints`.
    - The confirm button is disabled until the declaration is legal, with the reason shown.
  - Submit via `act`, which the contract validator accepts. `CombatTaxPayment` follows when Propaganda-style taxes apply.

### 10. Declaring blockers
- **How Arena works:**
  - Drag each blocker onto an attacker. [S]
  - Phone: tap the blocker, then the attacker. [S, official FAQ]
  - Multi-block uses a right-click-hold trick. [S]
  - Dragging a token pile's count blocks with all of them. [S]
  - Menace blocking is buggy. [S]
- **Build** (the data is `DeclareBlockers{valid_blocker_ids, valid_block_targets, block_requirements}`):
  - Showing the attackers: those coming at me sit in an "Incoming" row with each attacker's art; attacks aimed at other players are dimmed.
  - Assigning and removing blockers:
    - Drag a blocker onto an attacker, or click blocker then attacker. A blocker-to-attacker arrow is drawn.
    - Clicking an assigned blocker removes it.
  - Menace: a "needs 2 blockers" chip.
  - Buttons: primary "Block (2)" / "No blocks", secondary "Reset".

### 11. Combat damage assignment
- **How Arena works:**
  - The "Auto Assign Combat Damage" setting assigns lethal damage only, never extra. Turning it off brings up a manual screen. [S]
  - Since Foundations (12 November 2024) there is no damage assignment order. Damage is divided freely in the damage step. [S]
  - Patch 2024.44.00 replaced the shield marker with the opponent's avatar, and let a trampler blocked by one creature assign extra damage to it again. [S]
  - The exact controls are not documented. [M]
- **Build:**
  - Data: `AssignCombatDamage{total_damage, blockers[{blocker_id, lethal_minimum}], trample, pw_loyalty, assignment_modes}`.
  - Auto-submit the greedy split unless there are several blockers or trample with damage to spare. In those cases open a panel pre-filled with the greedy split, so one click on "Done" accepts it.
  - Panel layout:
    - The attacker at the top, with "5 to assign, 0 left".
    - One row per blocker with a "lethal 3" hint and minus/value/plus steppers. Clicking the card adds 1; right-click or long-press subtracts 1.
    - A trample row with the defending player's portrait.
  - Submit through `act`, because the option list only has the greedy split.

### 12. Stack and responding
- **How Arena works:**
  - The stack sits on the right. Items wait there while you can respond or have full control. [S]
  - Hover an item for its targets; right-click for the full card. [S]
  - An arrow collapses the stack (on phones it's at the top). Large stacks expand into the middle of the screen. [S]
  - The stack collapses automatically so targets are visible. [S]
  - Cards zoom in when they go on the stack. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Desktop:
    - A right rail. The top item is largest and labelled "Resolves next".
    - Each item shows the controller's colour and art chip, the name, and target chips.
    - Hover draws arrows to the targets (`StackTargetArcs`). Click opens the inspector.
  - When another player casts, the card is shown large in the centre for 600–900ms, then flies to the stack. Skip this for your own spells.
  - Show who currently holds priority (from `waiting_on`).
  - To respond, just cast; playable cards glow.
  - Phone: a strip above the dock with a count; tap it for the list.

### 13. Ordering triggers, "may" triggers, replacement effects
- **How Arena works:**
  - The "Auto Order Triggered Abilities" setting; guides recommend turning it off. [S]
  - Players complain the ordering UI doesn't say which trigger is which. [S]
  - The "Auto Choose Replacement Effect" setting. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Triggers:
    - Data: `OrderTriggers{triggers[{source_id, source_name, description}]}`.
    - A list from "Resolves first" at the top to "Resolves last" at the bottom.
    - Each row shows source art, name and the trigger's own text, with #1/#2 for duplicates.
    - Reorder with drag handles, or up/down buttons on phones.
    - Default to automatic ordering; always ask when full control is on.
    - Offer "Remember this order" (`SetTriggerOrderTemplate`).
  - "May" triggers: Yes/No plus "Always for this card this game" (`DecideOptionalEffectAndRemember`). Replacement effects work the same way.

### 14. Mulligan
- **How Arena works:**
  - "Keep" / "Mulligan". [S]
  - Brawl gives a free first mulligan. [S]
  - London mulligan: after keeping, you put cards on the bottom equal to the number of mulligans. [S]
  - The screen for picking bottom cards (pick cards, then "Done") is from memory. [M]
- **Build:**
  - Data: `MulliganDecision{pending, free_first_mulligan}`, then the `BottomCards{count}` phase. All players decide at the same time.
  - A large overlay that keeps opponents' status visible ("thinking", "kept", "mulliganed 1").
  - Buttons: primary "Keep 7", secondary "Mulligan (free)" or "Mulligan to 6". Optionally a small "3 lands" hint.
  - Bottom step:
    - Prompt: "Put 1 card on the bottom".
    - Clicking a card drops it into a "Bottom" tray in order; clicking it in the tray brings it back.
    - Button: "Done (1/1)".

### 15. Scry, surveil, looking at the top
- **How Arena works:**
  - Scry: cards left of a card-sleeve image go to the bottom; cards right of it stay on top, and the rightmost is the top card. [S]
  - Surveil: two boxes, "Library" and "Graveyard". Drag the cards, then "Done". [S]
  - Clicking your library shows the known positions of cards. [S]
- **Build:**
  - The response is `SelectCards{cards: keep-on-top in order}`, as in phase's `ReorderableTopChoice`. It needs `act` for partial splits.
  - Layout: two labelled drop zones ("Top" / "Bottom", or "Library" / "Graveyard"), drag between them, and drag to reorder within the top zone.
  - Phone: a toggle chip on each card plus up/down buttons.
  - Later: let players see known card positions on their own library.

### 16. Searching the library and choosing from lists
- **How Arena works:**
  - A card browser. The may-cast browser is headed "Select Card to Cast". [S]
  - The graveyard browser stays open while you make several picks. [S]
  - Arena makes repeated choices quick: Sylvan Library got a one-button flow, with an exact rules version only when cards like Ashiok are around. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Engine data: `SearchChoice{cards, count, up_to, constraint}` -> `SelectCards`. This must use `act`: the option list caps multi-card searches at 12 cards.
  - Browser:
    - A grid with a filter box and sorting by name or mana value.
    - Selected cards lift and get a check mark.
    - A "Find nothing" button when allowed.
    - Button: "Done (1/2)".
  - Hidden information: only the searcher gets the list; everyone else sees "Ana is searching their library".
  - Other lists:
    - Naming a card: a search box.
    - Choosing a colour: pip buttons.
    - Choosing a number: the same stepper as X.

### 17. Undo
- **How Arena works:**
  - Z undoes only actions that don't use the stack (mana abilities, tapping lands) and wrong targets, and only until priority is passed or the effect resolves. [S]
  - Mobile has a small undo button. [S]
- **Build:**
  - Undo in the client for anything still being put together: attacker or blocker selections, damage sliders, scry piles. Nothing is sent until you confirm.
  - Undo through the engine for `UntapLandForMana` and `CancelCast`.
  - After you pass priority, nothing can be undone, as in Arena.
  - Optional, beyond Arena: an "Ask to take back" option that needs every player's consent. Yama can rebuild the game by replaying the log without the last action, but only if no hidden information has come out since (no draw, shuffle or reveal).

### 18. Gameplay warnings
- **How Arena works:** "Enable Gameplay Warnings" asks you to confirm likely mistakes, such as aiming a damage spell at your own creature. [S]
- **Build:** a few confirmations behind a setting:
  - A harmful spell targeting your own permanent.
  - Choosing "No attacks" when you have creatures that could attack. phase asks for a second tap ("Tap Again: Attack with None").

## Keyboard (desktop) and gestures (phone)

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Space | Primary button |
| Enter | Pass until something happens (`UntilTurnBoundary EndOfCurrentTurn`; opponents' spells interrupt it) |
| Shift+Enter | Pass the turn unconditionally. phase has no exact equivalent, so this needs a per-seat Yama server flag. |
| Ctrl | Full control until you pass |
| Ctrl+Shift | Full control locked on |
| Z | Undo |
| Esc / right-click | Cancel |
| L | Show or hide stops |
| QQ / hold Q | Later: float all, quick tap |

On phones:

| Gesture | What it does |

| Tap | Select |
| Long-press | Inspect |
| Flick a hand card up | Play it |
| Long-press your avatar | Full control |

The screens need room for:
- A right-hand stack rail.
- A primary button bottom-right, plus a secondary button and a pass-turn toggle.
- A stop ladder beside my portrait and beside the active opponent's portrait.
- Opponent portraits (commander art) that can be clicked or dropped on for targets and attacks.
- An "Incoming" combat lane.
- An overlay layer for arrows.
- Banner space at top centre.
- Docked versions of all of these on the phone.

findings.findings_markdown:
# Feel and feedback: what MTG Arena does, what players say, and what Yama should build

Researched 2026-10-18. Reddit could not be reached (blocked to the fetcher, and the redlib mirrors didn't resolve). Player sentiment comes instead from Wizards' official feedback board (feedback.wizards.com, current posts from 2026), Steam review aggregates, MTG Arena Zone, Draftsim, MTGRocks, Hipsters of the Coast and published reviews. Anything marked **(memory)** is my recollection of the Arena client and was not confirmed online. Bryan can check those in his own Arena install (there's a checklist in section 10).

## 0. Six points that matter most

1. **Yama can't animate well from the current View stream alone.** The server publishes views on a tokio `watch` channel (`server/src/play.rs:53,140`), which keeps only the newest value. When an AI seat makes 5 moves in a row, a client may only ever see the last board, so diffing views drops the steps in between. The engine already returns typed events: `ActionResult.events: Vec<GameEvent>` (`yama-phase/crates/engine/src/types/game_state.rs:19509`). It also has a per-viewer filter, `engine::game::filter_events_for_viewer(events, state, viewer)` (`visibility.rs:3245`). Yama currently ignores the events and keeps only `log_entries` (`play/src/lib.rs:541`). **Build an ordered event feed per seat.** That is the foundation for everything below.
2. **phase's own client already contains a complete animation and audio system**, and phase is MIT/Apache dual-licensed. The timing constants, event grouping, speed slider and audio buses can be ported straight into Yama's lighter board. There are details and numbers in section 1. Check the audio file licences before reusing the `.m4a`/`.mp3` files: the repo doesn't say what they are.
3. **Arena's biggest polish gap is your best chance to beat it.** Arena has no in-game game log or match history, and players lean on third-party trackers to get one. Yama already has a log and a replay log. Make them rich: hoverable card names, filters by category, turn dividers, and a step-through replay.
4. **Animations must never block input or cost someone time.** Current Arena feedback-board complaints include:
   - trigger animations that run out the turn timer (a Tainted Pact chain, a Breach the Multiverse loop);
   - a 250-creature attack the defender couldn't speed through;
   - pet-click animations that lagged opponents into timing out (about 50 players were banned in July 2019);
   - effects covering game information: the Amonkhet battlefield's sand hiding a graveyard in 2024, and flashback cards covering the life total.

   Yama needs a global speed slider, a skip button, automatic catch-up, and a hard rule that effects never cover life totals or zones.
5. **Scryfall's image rules limit what effects are allowed** (scryfall.com/docs/api, fetched 2026-10-18):
   - "Do not distort, skew, or stretch card images."
   - "Do not blur, sharpen, desaturate, or color-shift card images."
   - "When using the art_crop, list the artist name and copyright elsewhere in the same interface."

   So:
   - The commander-art background Bryan likes can't be blurred or desaturated.
   - No grey-out for dead or unplayable cards.
   - No shatter, burn or dissolve shaders applied to the card image itself.
   - The current `.tile.tapped img { filter: brightness(0.8) }` in `web/src/play/board.css` is probably a colour shift; replace it with a badge or angle-only styling.
6. **Arena has no four-player mode** as far as I know (its Brawl is 1v1), so it offers no model for focusing attention, aiming attacks across seats, or tracking commander damage in a pod. Those need their own design (section 8).

## 1. Engineering foundation: an event feed per seat, plus phase's animation system

### What the engine gives us (checked in `../yama-phase`)

- **Event types.** `GameEvent` has about 95 variants, including:
  - `SpellCast`, `StackPushed`/`StackResolved`, `ZoneChanged{object_id, from, to}`
  - `CardDrawn`, `LandPlayed`, `TokenCreated{object_id, name}`, `CreatureDestroyed`, `PermanentSacrificed`
  - `DamageDealt{source_id, target, amount, is_combat, excess}`
  - `LifeChanged{player_id, amount, …}`, which carries the resulting total "so a presentation layer animating a run of life changes can show each intermediate total"
  - `CombatDamageDealtToPlayer{source_amounts, total_damage}`, `AttackersDeclared{attacker_ids, defending_player, attacks}`, `BlockersDeclared{assignments}`
  - `BecomesTarget{target, source_id}`, `CounterAdded`/`CounterRemoved`, `PermanentTapped`/`PermanentUntapped`, `Transformed`
  - `TurnStarted`, `PhaseChanged`, `PlayerEliminated`, `GameOver`
- **Log entries are already structured.** `GameLogEntry` has `segments: Vec<LogSegment>`, where a segment is `Text`, `CardName{name, object_id}`, `PlayerName`, `Number`, `Mana`, `Zone` or `Keyword`. Each entry also has a `category` (Combat, Stack, Life, Zone, Token, Trigger, Destroy, …) and a `presentation` (importance Essential/Context/Detail/Diagnostic, tone, visibility). Yama's `segments_text()` flattens all of that to plain text and keeps only Essential lines. Send the segments to the client instead.
- **Dry runs for "what if" previews.** `engine::game::preview` (issue #5468) does a non-mutating dry run of an action. It returns public deltas — life changes, public zone moves, tokens created, objects that ceased to exist — and is meant for hover previews like "this kills that" or "you take 4". It is hidden-information safe because it diffs states that have already been filtered for the viewer.
- **Commander and damage helpers.** `commander_lethal_headroom()` (`game/commander.rs:102`) and `lethal_damage_needed()` (`combat_damage.rs:1469`, which accounts for deathtouch).

### Wire design (suggested)

- **Server side.** In `Match::accepted`, also take `result.events`, filter them per seat with `filter_events_for_viewer`, and then map them into Yama's own small `AnimEvent` type using a whitelist. Don't send raw engine events: ARCHITECTURE already warns that phase's filtered state still names opponents' library cards internally.
- **Ring buffer.** Store `{seq, revision, events}` in a buffer per match (for example the last 1,000 events).
- **Client side.**
  - The client tracks `lastSeq`. Each `view` message carries `events: AnimEvent[]` for every seq after the last one sent, or the client asks for them.
  - If there's a gap (after a reconnect), snap straight to the view without animating.
  - If the view arrives with no events, render it as it is now.
- **View is always the truth.** Animations play from the events, then the board settles on the View. If the person makes a decision while animations are still queued, finish the queue and jump to the final state.

### What to port from phase's client (`yama-phase/client/src/animation/`, `components/animation/`, `audio/`)

- **Durations** (`animation/types.ts`, in ms at speed 1.0):

  | Event | Duration (ms) |
  |---|---|
  | `ZoneChanged` | 400 |
  | `SpellCast` | 500 |
  | `DamageDealt` (combat engagement) | 900 |
  | `LifeChanged` | 300 |
  | `CreatureDestroyed` | 400 |
  | `TokenCreated` | 400 |
  | `CounterAdded` / `CounterRemoved` | 200 |
  | `PermanentTapped` / `PermanentUntapped` | 200 |
  | Card slam flight before impact | 200 |
  | Damage projectile (fireball, lightning) to impact | 440 |
  | Turn banner | 1,500 |
  | Default | 200 |

- **Grouping:**
  - 8 or more similar events in a row collapse into one beat, so 8+ tokens animate once.
  - 12 or more combat damage events become one "damage flurry" lasting 900 ms, with 8 to 32 projectiles and at most 96 trail particles.
- **Non-visual events** that get no animation step: `PriorityPassed`, `ManaAdded`, `CardDrawn`/`CardsDrawn` (the paired `ZoneChanged` animates instead), `StackPushed`/`StackResolved`, `Milled`, `AttackersDeclared`/`BlockersDeclared`, `CombatDamageDealtToPlayer`, and mana abilities.
- **Step rules:**
  - `SpellCast` and `TurnStarted` always start a new step.
  - `ZoneChanged` and `LifeChanged` merge into the step before them.
  - A life change lands exactly when the hit that caused it lands (`lifeChangeImpactDelayMs`), so the number, the flash and the impact effect happen together.
- **Speed settings:**
  - A global multiplier from 0 to 2 in steps of 0.05, where 0 means instant.
  - Separate multipliers for "effects", "combat" and "banners".
  - Effects quality: `full`, `reduced` or `minimal`. On touch devices the canvas pixel ratio is capped lower.
- **Building blocks:**
  - `FloatingNumber`: rises 60 px and fades over 0.8 s, starts at scale 1.2, bold text with a dark shadow.
  - `DamageVignette`, `ScreenShake`, `TurnBanner`, `CastArcAnimation`, `CardSlamAnimation`, `DeathShatter`.
  - `hiddenDocumentMotion`: turns off CSS animations while the tab is hidden, which avoids a Chromium memory leak with detached animations.
- **Audio** (`AudioManager`): Web Audio with master/SFX/music gains, an SFX file for each event type (14 sounds), music chosen by context (menu, lobby, battlefield, victory, defeat), and early/mid/late battlefield tracks switching at turns 5 and 10.
- **Caveat:** the shatter, burn and dissolve shaders (`cardVfx/cardShatter.ts`, `cardBurn.ts`, `exileDissolve.ts`) apply effects to the card image itself, which conflicts with Scryfall's no-distort and no-colour-shift rules.
- **No new dependency needed.** Yama's web app has no animation library (React 19 and Vite only). The Web Animations API (`el.animate`) plus FLIP (measure each card's rectangle by card id before and after, then animate a transform between them) covers this.

## 2. Pacing, timing and skipping

**What Arena does and what's been changed**

- Arena's principal designer Chris Clay says animations should "do their job and then get out of the way". The goal is "getting Magic to play snappy… with all of those complex rules", and Duels of the Planeswalkers is cited as a game whose animations ran too long (PCGamesN).
- Patch 0.9.0 (Nov 2018):
  - "Reduced the minimum amount of time for an opponent's spell or ability on the stack from 1 second to 0.4 seconds".
  - "Thousand-Year Storm's VFX block from 1 second to 0.25 seconds".
  - "Players gain additional time after selecting targets for triggered abilities".
  - "When you have a decision to make and are alt-tabbed off, the Arena taskbar icon will flash".
- Jan 2021: "Exile animations, particularly when being done to pay a cost, have been sped up."
- Mar 2021: "Even more improvements to performance around animating huge stacks of stuff."
- MTG Arena Zone advises players to set stops early "since the server can run ahead of the animations." Arena's state runs ahead and its animations trail behind.
- Comparable games:
  - Hearthstone cut minion trigger resolution from 0.8 s to 0.2 s, with flagged special cases at 0 s, to match Battlegrounds pacing.
  - A Legends of Runeterra player complained after a speed-up that it felt "too fast" and inconsistent because "not all animations were sped up". The player asked Riot to "pause the timer during animations".

**What players complain about**

All of these are current feedback.wizards.com posts:

- "Option to speed up or entirely skip long sets of triggers & animations".
- Pact trigger animations don't pause the turn timer, which caused timeouts.
- A Breach the Multiverse loop timed out "due to long animations".
- An opponent attacked with 250+ creatures and the defender had no way to speed it up.
- "Flashback Cards Are Obscuring My Life Total".
- A lemm.ee post, which cites a Wizards feedback suggestion, asks for "greater control over the amount of animation in Arena", including turning off sleeves, card styles, pets and background effects.

As far as I could find, Arena has no animation-speed slider.

**What to build**

- Global "Animation speed" slider, Instant to 2x (default 1x), plus separate sliders for effects, combat and banners (as phase has).
- **Skip.** Space, Esc, or a tap on the board while animations are queued finishes the queue at once. Show a small "Skip ▸▸" chip while the queue is longer than about 1 s.
- **Automatic catch-up.**
  - If more than about 2.5 s of animation is queued, play the rest at 2x; above about 6 s, collapse straight to the final state.
  - When the tab is hidden, apply events without animating.
  - In a four-player game, animations from opponents interacting with each other, where you're not involved, play at about 0.6x their normal duration.
- **Minimum reading time.** An opponent's or AI's spell stays on the stack at least 400 ms (Arena's number), or 800 to 1,000 ms if it targets you or your permanents. AI seats act instantly, so without this floor their turns become an unreadable blur.
- **Input is never locked.** The decision panel works while animations play. If you act, the queue finishes immediately.
- **No timer pressure.** If Yama ever adds a turn clock, pause it during animations and during the other players' decisions.
- **Triggers:** 150 to 200 ms each, with runs of 8 or more batched into one beat (Hearthstone and phase numbers).

## 3. Card motion: draw, cast, stack, resolve, enter the battlefield, death

**What Arena does**

- **Hand:** cards sit at the bottom with their lower halves cut off, and hovering brings a card fully on screen. Cards playable from the graveyard or exile sit to the right, separated by a gap (Hipsters 2018; MTG Arena Zone).
- **Casting:** drag the card upward or double-click it. While you hover or drag, Arena highlights the lands it plans to tap (MTG Arena Zone).
- **Stack:** sits on the right as large cards. Hovering a stack item shows its targets, and the item's text is coloured to match its targeting line; the colours were chosen to work with colour blindness (patch 0.9.0). A very large stack expands into the middle of the screen, and a small arrow can collapse the stack panel.
- **Mythic effects:** Game Informer praised "flashy enter-the-battlefield effects for mythic cards". Early mythics had bespoke animations; MTGRocks says these "became a thing of the past" as cosmetics took over development time. A 2025 player comment praised a set's animations as "tastefully short so as to not waste too much time".
- **(memory)** Creatures drop onto the battlefield with a weighty thud and dust ring. Destroyed creatures break up and fly to the graveyard. Exiled cards fade into light. Draws fly from the library to the hand.

**What to build** (times at 1x speed)

| Beat | Motion | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Your draw | Card flies from the library to its hand slot. A burst of draws staggers 80 ms per card, and 4 or more draws fan in together. | 300 ms |
| Opponent draw | Card back flies into their panel and the hand count ticks up. No face shown. | 200 ms |
| Land play | Slam into the lands row, thud sound, tiny dust ring drawn around (not over) the card. | 200 ms flight + 120 ms impact |
| Cast | Card lifts from the hand or seat panel along an arc to the stack panel. The targeting line draws from the stack card to each target. | 400 to 500 ms |
| Stack resolve, permanent | Card flies from the stack to its battlefield slot (FLIP), then slams. | 200 ms flight + 150 ms impact |
| Stack resolve, instant or sorcery | Effect plays (projectile, then impact), then the card shrinks into its owner's graveyard pile. | 440 ms to impact + 250 ms |
| Countered | Card shakes, then drops to the graveyard; "Countered" label on the stack. | 400 ms |
| Token | Pops in at its slot: scale 0.85 to 1, opacity 0 to 1. Batch 8 or more. | 250 to 400 ms |
| Dies | Card lifts slightly, a puff of particles plays around it, then it flies to the graveyard pile. The whole card moves as one piece; no shader on the image. | 400 ms |
| Exiled | Same, but it fades out with a light ring and goes to the exile pile. | 400 ms |
| Tap / untap | Rotate 90° (Yama already has a 140 ms transition, which is fine). Untap step: everything untaps together. | 200 ms |
| Counter added | Badge pops (scale 1.3 to 1) and its number ticks. | 200 ms |

Battlefield cards are grouped into piles in Yama (`piles()` in `Board.tsx`). Give each animated card an id-keyed DOM rectangle or anchor so a card can fly out of a pile. When a pile's count changes, pulse the count badge.

## 4. Combat: attacking, blocking, damage, lethal preview

**What Arena does**

- Click creatures to choose attackers. Click the number on a stack of identical creatures to send the whole stack, or select several and then pick their target. Hover the defending player to see which attackers are still unblocked.
- In the damage step, "a creature whose damage equals its toughness shows its power in blue" — a lethal-assignment cue (MTG Arena Zone). Marked damage shows as lowered toughness.
- The phase strip has stop icons for combat steps: a sword for declare attackers, a shield for declare blockers, an explosion for damage.
- Settings include "Auto Assign Combat Damage".
- **(memory)** A context button at the bottom right reads "All Attack" / "No Attacks", then "No Blocks" / "Done". Attackers tilt forward. Blockers move in front of their attacker. In the damage step, creatures lunge at their target.
- I couldn't find any Arena feature that warns "this attack is lethal" or "this block kills your creature". Legends of Runeterra-style outcome previews don't exist in Arena.

**What to build**

- **Declaring attackers (multiplayer).**
  - Tap a creature to toggle it as an attacker; it slides 12 px toward the opponents' area and gets a red edge.
  - With more than one possible defender, the attacker gets a target chip ("→ Alice"). Change it by tapping an opponent's panel while the attacker is selected, or by dragging (desktop).
  - Buttons: "Attack with all → [opponent]", "No attacks", "Confirm (n)".
  - The engine's options already list every legal attack, so these controls just pick among them.
- **Incoming summary on each opponent panel:** "⚔ 3 attackers · 9 damage". When it's you being attacked, your own panel shows the same summary in red, and **"LETHAL"** if unblocked damage ≥ your life. Also warn on commander damage: "Atraxa: 18 → 24 of 21". The commander-damage numbers come from `commander_damage` in the view and `commander_lethal_headroom` in the engine.
- **Blocking.** Tap your creature, then tap the attacker. A shield badge and a short connector line appear. With several blockers on one attacker, show the attacker's damage split, defaulting to the engine's automatic assignment.
- **Outcome preview** (goes beyond Arena). Add a server endpoint, `preview`, that:
  1. clones the game state;
  2. applies the candidate attack or block;
  3. passes priority for everyone through combat damage;
  4. diffs the result with `engine::game::preview`.

  Show the result as a ghost overlay — a skull badge on creatures that would die, "−5" on players — labelled "If no one responds". On desktop, run it on hover; on phones, once you've chosen. Limit to about 5 previews per second per seat; the engine clone is cheap compared with a full AI search.
- **Damage step.** Each attacker lunges 20 px toward its target (120 ms out, 180 ms back) and hits at the peak, followed by an impact flash, a floating number and a life tick. Use phase's combat engagement time of 900 ms per exchange. With first strike or double strike, play two waves. Trample sends the excess damage on to the player as a second floating number.

## 5. Damage numbers, life totals, highlights, hover preview

### Life and damage

- Arena reviews praise the damage effects ("effects… explode when you cast spells and do damage", Pocket Gamer 2021). **(memory)** Arena's avatar life total flashes and ticks.
- **Build:**
  - `FloatingNumber` at the target: −N red or +N green/gold, rising 60 px over 0.8 s.
  - The life number ticks through each total the engine reports, at 300 ms per change, with a background flash. Loss is red (#E5484D), gain is green (#3FB950). Pair the colour with a "−"/"+" sign and a down/up arrow, so colour isn't the only signal.
  - When **you** take 5 or more damage, add a light red edge vignette (phase's `DamageVignette`) and a 4 px, 150 ms shake. Turn the shake off with reduced motion.
  - Lifelink: 6 to 10 particles travel from the source creature to its controller's life total, and the gain number arrives with them.
  - Creature damage: the toughness number turns red and shows remaining toughness (Yama's `.stat.hurt` already does this). The full sheet adds "2 damage marked".

### Playable highlights

- Arena: "Cards you can play with your available mana get a blue outline" (Hipsters 2018). Players have complained that some ability highlights "glow constantly" (Steam thread, per a search summary).
- **Build:** Yama already knows which cards have options (`byCard`).
  - Hand cards with options: a blue outline, for example `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #4DA3FF, 0 0 14px 2px rgb(77 163 255 / .55)`. Breathe it once on a new decision (1.2 s), then leave it steady. Don't loop the pulse.
  - Battlefield permanents with options get a thinner steady outline.
  - Keep the existing dot or a small "bolt" icon, so the cue doesn't rely on colour.
  - Never filter the image itself.

### Targeting

- **Build:** when every option in a decision is a target choice:
  - Valid targets get an amber outline (#F5A524) plus a crosshair badge. Everything else stays as it is: don't dim the images.
  - Hovering or selecting a target draws an SVG line from the source (the stack card, or the card being cast) to the target, coloured by the source player's seat colour.
  - Selected targets get a solid white outline with a check badge.
  - Lines on the stack stay visible while the item is on the stack, and stack text in the same colour echoes the line (as Arena does).
- If targeting by tap is the only way, show a prompt line: "Choose a target for Lightning Bolt (1 of 1)".

### Hover and inspection

- **Arena:**
  - Hovering a hand card brings it fully on screen.
  - Battlefield cards show "mostly art and ability symbols", with ability icons along the lower edge and an ellipsis when there are too many.
  - Hovering shows the full card. "Keyword Reminders" (on by default) adds floating keyword explanations.
  - Right-click shows full details, including on stack items. Mobile uses press-and-hold: a current iOS bug report complains that "holding a card no longer zooms" in the deck builder.
- Text-size complaints: wordy cards stay hard to read even zoomed, and players ask for scrollable text with scalable font (MTGRocks 2021 and 2023).
- **Build:**
  - Desktop hover delay 150 ms. Place the preview on the side away from the pointer, at 300 to 360 px wide.
  - Next to it, a keyword panel with one line per keyword: "Flying: can't be blocked except by creatures with flying or reach". This needs a `keywords` list in `CardView`.
  - Show the current power/toughness against the printed values, counters, attachments, and "summoning sick".
  - Hovering a card name in the log or on the stack shows the same preview.
  - Phones: tap to select or filter (current behaviour); long-press 350 ms opens the card sheet, with `navigator.vibrate(10)` on Android.
  - In the sheet, oracle text is real text that follows the text-size setting (avoids Arena's complaint).

## 6. Turn and phase indicator, stops, notifications, game log

### Phase ladder and passing

- **Arena:**
  - A phase strip next to each portrait; the current phase is lit orange.
  - Click a phase to set a stop. Orange stops apply on your turn, blue on opponents'.
  - Shortcuts:

    | Key | Action |
    |---|---|
    | L | Show or hide phases |
    | Ctrl | Full control for this phase |
    | Shift+Ctrl | Full control until turned off |
    | Enter | Pass until something you could respond to |
    | Shift+Enter / F6 | Pass the turn |
    | Space | Pass priority |
    | Z | Undo mana taps |
    | QQ | Tap all mana sources |

- **Complaints** (current feedback board):
  - auto-pass "Skipped my ability to respond before combat";
  - "Combat phase skipped with Great Train Heist in hand";
  - "Upkeep pause after milling out", asking for an automatic stop at upkeep when the library is empty;
  - the Enter key was remapped so that it "passes the turn and gets hit accidentally".

  Auto-passing is the area most likely to cost someone a game.
- **Build** on Yama's existing smart stops:
  - Make the existing `PhaseTrack` steps clickable stop toggles, with two rows: "my turn" and "others' turns". Save them per user.
  - A visible pass-state chip: "Passing to your turn · Stop". Pressing it cancels.
  - Shortcuts: Space passes once. Shift+Enter passes to your turn and shows a 2 s undo toast. Hold Ctrl for full control for the current step.
  - Add a smart stop for "my library is empty and I'm about to draw".
  - The main button's label follows the context: "Pass", "Resolve", "To combat", "End turn", "Confirm attackers (3)", "No blocks".

### Turn start and decision alerts

- Arena flashes the taskbar icon when you have a decision and are alt-tabbed away (patch 0.9.0).
- **Build:**
  - On your turn: a 900 ms "Your turn" banner. Phase uses 1,500 ms, which is too long when a pod has four turns per round.
  - Other players' turns: a small non-blocking toast.
  - When a decision arrives:
    - always play a soft ping;
    - if `document.hidden`: change `document.title` to "(!) Your move · Yama", set a badge with the Badging API, send a `Notification` (Yama is an installable web app), and vibrate on Android.
  - The active seat's panel gets a glowing border in its seat colour. Seats the game is waiting on show the existing "deciding…" pulse.

### Game log and history

- **Arena:**
  - "MTG Arena still offers no complete built-in match history or replay viewer" (Out of Games, 2026).
  - Draftsim: "you can't check this in MTGA itself".
  - Players rely on Arena Tutor, 17Lands and Untapped reading the client's Detailed Logs. On the official forum, players have asked for a button showing the last spell an opponent cast.
  - Feedback-board bug reports now link 17Lands game histories as evidence.
- **Build:**
  1. Keep the `LogSegment`s and render card names as hoverable chips showing the card image, and player names in seat colours.
  2. Filters by category: Combat, Stack, Life, Zone, Tokens, Triggers. Show Essential entries by default, with a "Details" toggle that also shows Context and Detail.
  3. A turn divider: "Turn 7 · Alice".
  4. A "Since your last turn" summary per opponent at the start of your turn ("Bob: cast Cultivate, attacked you for 5").
  5. A strip of the last 5 resolved spells/abilities as thumbnails along the board edge, to answer "what just happened?"; tap one to see its card and targets.
  6. A step-through replay from the replay log Yama already saves (turn scrubber, play/pause at speed).

  Arena has none of these.
